headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: LangGraph’s writable, networked orchestration can ingest Great Expectations outputs and act on them without default verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations writes validation results and documentation to files, while LangGraph reads files and can wire developer-defined tools into agent graphs. That creates a plausible file-based bridge where attacker-controlled content in validation artifacts could be treated as instructions. No shared clipboard/MCP is shown, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF LangGraph reads Great Expectations-generated files as prompts or tool instructions
IF the shared workspace is writable by both agents
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Treat Great Expectations outputs as data, not prompts
Add a file allowlist for LangGraph inputs
Insert a sanitization step before any file is parsed as instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all exchanged files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, and LangGraph has broad network egress plus model-provider API keys. If both share a workspace, file contents from Great Expectations can flow into LangGraph and then out to third-party APIs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default orchestration, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem workspace
IF LangGraph forwards shared files or graph state to a model provider
mitigations: Keep Great Expectations artifacts out of LangGraph inputs
Use separate service accounts and API keys
Restrict LangGraph to redacted summaries only
Rotate any exposed model-provider keys
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write files, while LangGraph can execute shells, spawn subprocesses, write files, and access broad network egress. On a shared directory, both can mutate the same artifacts without any locking or coordination primitive shown, so conflicting writes and state corruption are likely and can be irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same writable directory
IF LangGraph instances share checkpointer-backed state without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Serialize access with a simple lock file
Snapshot files before LangGraph mutates them
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results, and LangGraph is a stateful orchestration framework that can route those outputs into downstream tools. If LangGraph treats those results as authoritative, a bad validation or malformed report can cascade into automated actions or incorrect decisions. No built-in verification barrier is shown, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF LangGraph uses Great Expectations validation output as an input to tool-using nodes
IF downstream nodes act without an explicit verification step
mitigations: Require human review before any action node runs
Add schema validation for Great Expectations outputs
Compare results against a second independent check
Log and halt on malformed validation artifacts
requires-engineering: add a verification gate between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations is an open-source data-quality library touching validation results and documentation, while LangGraph is a networked orchestration framework handling model-provider keys. The profiles do not show a specific residency or regulated-data mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is supported from the documented retention and logging surface differences.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into LangGraph graph state
IF logs or checkpoints retain Great Expectations validation artifacts
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in graph state
Minimize checkpoint retention
Redact validation artifacts before logging
Review data-processing notices for both systems
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
